text:
alex: Heads-up — getting a few customer reports that quota enforcement is lagging and letting short bursts through. Billing shows tokens consumed but the per-key limiter still allowed traffic for ~60–120s. Anyone else seeing this?

marta: yep, saw it around 10:12 UTC on the shared pool. Ingestion to the metering store is ~90s behind for some shards. enforcement queries the store directly so it undercounts during the lag.

cheng: quick summary of root cause I see: the metering pipeline acks at handoff to Kafka -> consumers do async writes to clickhouse. Enforcement queries ClickHouse replica that lags under backpressure.

cheng: snippet of the read we do today:

```sql
SELECT sum(tokens) FROM usage_by_key WHERE org_id = ? AND ts >= toStartOfInterval(now() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR, INTERVAL 1 MINUTE)
```

cheng: that aggregate is eventually correct but not useful for sub-minute enforcement.

sara: customers are hitting spiky workloads (webhooks/cron fans). They see 200s for a minute then 429s after enforcement catches up => confused on pricing. We need both a short-term fix and a long-term reconciliation plan.

alex: short-term mitigations: 1) edge token-buckets (in-memory) per-key with small burst window, 2) switch enforcement to read from the write-ahead cache (ingestion buffer) for last 2 minutes, or 3) soft-deny mode that returns 200 with X-RateLimit-Warning header and throttles on subsequent requests. Which is fastest to ship?

marta: fastest is edge token-buckets; we already have lite-buckets in the gateway code. We can enable them for impacted orgs via a flag. That prevents the "let it all through then charge" pattern.

devex: for UX in Console, can we show a "realtime enforcement lag" badge on the quota page and a tooltip explaining soft-deny vs hard-deny? That will cut down support tickets.

cheng: long-term: make enforcement fallback to the ingestion buffer (redis stream) which has near-real-time counts. Plan: 1) expose a last_committed_offset per-shard, 2) have enforcement read incremental deltas from buffer for the last 2 minutes, 3) reconcile to clickhouse every 5–10m. Reconciliation should publish compensating metrics to billing pipeline.

marta: also add a metric enforcement.metering_lag_seconds with tags {shard, org_id} and alert if >30s for any shard for >5m.

alex: agree. For rollout: canary the edge bucket enable for 5 high-usage beta orgs, then flip more. Need an on/off runtime feature flag.

deploy-bot: Started canary deploy: gateway/feature/edge-buckets -> 3 instances in us-west2. Canary window 15m.

cheng: reconciliation pseudo:

```py
# run every 10m
deltas = read_buffer_deltas(since=last_reconcile)
for (org, key), tokens in deltas.items():
    write_compensating_record_to_clickhouse(org, key, tokens)
    emit_metric('reconcile.tokens', tokens, tags={'org': org})
```

cheng: make sure reconciliation only writes positive deltas and guards against double-counting using idempotent write keys.

sara: action items?

alex: 1) marta -> enable edge buckets behind flag and ship canary (ETA 3h) 2) cheng -> prototype reading from ingestion buffer and reconciliation job (ETA EOD) 3) devex -> add enforcement-lag indicator mock for Console (ETA tomorrow) 4) ops -> add enforcement.metering_lag_seconds alert (ETA 1h)

marta: doing canary now, will post results in this thread.

quota-bot: Warning: org-2849 exceeded soft-burst allowance 2025-11-30T10:25:12Z :exclamation:

alex: thanks. If canary looks good we'll also tweak default burst per-org (reduce for low-tier) and add a note to pricing page about burst allowances.

marta: canary looks stable — no billing anomalies during the 15m window. Will expand to 10% traffic next.

cheng: I'll push a PR for the buffer-read shim, linking the reconciliation job. Putting it in staging for integration tests.

sara: great, please add a short blurb for support playbook so CS can explain behavior when enforcement lags.

alex: closing loop later today — we'll keep this thread for postmortem notes. Thanks all!
